title: US STOCKS-Tech stocks pressure Wall St; Apple down ahead of event
text:
Shutterstock photo
(For a live blog on the U.S. stock market, click LIVE/ ortype LIVE/ in an Eikon news window.)
* Apple, Alphabet, Amazon drop on news of Senate testimony
* Apple down ahead of expected iPhones launch at 1 pm ET
* Energy stocks gain as oil prices push above $80 a barrel
* Indexes: Dow up 0.35 pct; S&P off 0.02 pct, Nasdaq down0.48 pct (Updates to early afternoon)
By Shreyashi Sanyal
Sept 12 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq fell on Wednesday, weigheddown by a drop in Apple on fears of further regulation, while arise in energy stocks and a report of fresh U.S.-China tradetalks helped keep the S&P afloat and boost Dow Industrials.
Six major web and internet service companies, includingApple AAPL.O , are to detail their consumer data privacypractices to a U.S. Senate panel on Sept. 26, raising thespecter of the possibility of stricter regulation. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL2N1VY0O6
Apple was down 1 percent, weighing the most on the threemajor indexes. The stock was trading higher premarket, ahead ofan event at 1 p.m. ET (1700 GMT) where the company is expectedto launch new iPhone models as well as upgrades of otherproducts. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL2N1VY0KL
Twitter TWTR.N , Alphabet GOOGL.O and Amazon.comAMZN.O , among the six companies to testify, were tradingbetween flat and down 4.2 percent.
Facebook FB.O , not among the companies to testify, wasdown 2 percent. The S&P technology sector .SPLRCT fell 0.64percent.
"Headlines like the Senate hearing does add this element ofregulatory risk to Apple and Amazon which is what could bedriving them lower right now," said Mark Heppenstall, chiefinvestment officer at Penn Mutual Asset Management in Horsham,Pennsylvania.
The markets got a boost from a Wall Street Journal reportthat said Washington has proposed a new round of trade talkswith Beijing before the Trump administration implementsadditional tariffs on Chinese imports.
Also helping was the energy sector .SPNY , which jumped0.70 percent as Brent crude price pushed above $80 a barrel dueto growing concerns over global oil supply. O/R
At 12:41 a.m. ET the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI wasup 91.95 points, or 0.35 percent, at 26,063.01, the S&P 500 .SPX was down 0.60 points, or 0.02 percent, at 2,887.29 andthe Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was down 38.20 points, or 0.48percent, at 7,934.28.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor index .SOX was down 1.8percent after Goldman Sachs became the latest brokerage to warnof lower prices for memory chips due to an oversupply of DRAMand NAND chips.
Micron MU.O slid 5 percent, the most on the S&P. Chipequipment makers were hit the hardest, falling in a range ofApplied Materials' AMAT.O 2 percent drop and Entegris'sENTG.O 4.4 percent decline.
The consumer staples sector .SPLRCS rose 1.20 percent asAltria MO.N jumped 7.2 percent and Philip Morris InternationalPM.N gained 4 percent.
Traders said that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration'sproposed ban on flavored e-cigarettes was less harsh thanfeared. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL2N1VY0RK
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners for a 1.29-to-1 ratioon the NYSE. Declining issues outnumbered advancers for a1.41-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 29 new 52-week highs and six newlows, while the Nasdaq recorded 61 new highs and 76 new lows. (Reporting by Shreyashi Sanyal in Bengaluru; Editing by ArunKoyyur and Shounak Dasgupta) (( Shreyashi.Sanyal@thomsonreuters.com ; +1 646 223 8780 ;Reuters Messaging: Shreyashi.Sanyal.thomsonreuters.com@reuters.net ))
